newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus opposition chief arrested ahead of protest.
newsitem.headline: Belarus opposition chief arrested ahead of protest.

text.p: Police arrested an opposition leader in Belarus overnight as he prepared for a street protest against President Alexander Lukashenko, officials of the opposition Popular Front group said on Friday.

Leader of the group, Professor Yuri Khodyko, 53, who spent 20 days in prison last year for helping to organise other anti-Lukashenko actions, was detained at the Front's office, a group spokesman said.
The spokesman said activists tried to resist when a group of uniformed and plain-clothed police officers broke into their headquarters. One person was injured.
There was no immediate word from the police, who have stepped up action against opposition groups in recent days ahead of Constitution Day on Saturday, when a big rally is planned.
Another rally is planned for Friday afternoon.
About 100 people were detained after scuffles at a protest of several thousand people on March 10.
That protest was directed against the arrival of a delegation of Russian deputies to discuss integration between the neighbouring states.
Opposition officials said at least two protesters were beaten by police including another Front leader, Lyavon Barshchevski.
Anti-Lukashenko activists say the former Soviet republic faces a "political spring" this year.
Lukashenko has adopted an increasingly authoritarian style, assuming sweeping powers and rewriting his country's constitution after a referendum in November which he won by a landslide.
Most of the 10 million Belarussians back the former farm boss but an active group of nationalists, intellectuals and students concentrated in the capital oppose him.
Lukashenko and Russian President Boris Yeltsin signed a deal last year on creating a "community" and agreed to step up moves towards closer union when they met in Moscow on March 7.
Lukashenko has faced sharp criticism from the West for his authoritarian style and international lending bodies have suspended credits to Belarus pending faster economic reforms.
